newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Izetbegovic wins top seat in Bosnian presidency.
newsitem.headline: Izetbegovic wins top seat in Bosnian presidency.

text.p: Bosnia's Moslem President Alija Izetbegovic narrowly defeated hardline Bosnian Serb rival Momcilo Krajisnik to become the first head of Bosnia's new collective presidency, election scrutineers announced on Wednesday.
The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which organised the election, said the completed count gave Izetbegovic 729,034 votes and Krajisnik 690,373.
The third seat on the three-man presidency went to Bosnian Croat candidate Kresimir Zubak who won 342,077 votes. The result was unofficial pending certification.
The three men did not stand against each other but competed against rivals from within their own ethnic communities.
It was agreed that the candidate with the highest personal score would be the senior presidency member.
OSCE mission chief Robert Frowick told reporters: "It appears clear that President Izetbegovic will serve as the president of the presidency."
Izetbegovic, challenged hard by Krajisnik who is a strong supporter of Bosnian Serb independence, will effectively be Bosnia's head of state for the next two years.
The period will be crucial to prospects for the country's reunification under the 1995 Dayton peace agreement which ended 43 months of war.

The OSCE said former Bosnian prime minister Haris Silajdzic, who stood against Izetbegovic, won 123,784 votes, Mladen Ivan who stood against Krajisnik won 305,083 and Ivo Komsic who challenged Zubak won 38,261.
Although Moslems are the largest ethnic grouping in Bosnia, the combined vote for the two Moslem candidates was only 814,157 compared with 995,456 for the two Bosnian Serbs.
But the International Crisis Group (ICG) which helped monitor the elections, held last Saturday, said there was no evidence the Serbs had rigged the vote on their side.
The OSCE also announced that the same Serb, Croat and Moslem nationalist parties that helped ignite the war in Bosnia were leading in parliamentary elections carried out simultaneously last Saturday.

The Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA), the hardline Serb Democratic Party (SDS) and the Croat Democratic Union (HDZ) were ahead in the race for the 42-member joint House of Representatives, the organisers reported.
